newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Ex-Soviet Belarus to start WTO entry talks.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Soviet Belarus to start WTO entry talks.

text.p: Belarus, widely regarded as among the most reluctant reformers in the former Soviet Union, opens talks this week to try to win membership of the World Trade Organisation (WTO), officials said on Monday.

They said a delegation from Minsk would hold two days of talks on Thursday and Friday with a WTO working party which is likely to involve key trading powers including the United States, the European Union and Japan.

Reports from Minsk said the Belarus delegation was likely to be headed by Prime Minister Sergei Ling, a close ally of hardline President Alexander Lukashenko who is seeking to reshape a union with Russia.

But trade diplomats said the talks were only exploratory and marked the beginning of what was likely to be a prolonged process likely to last two to three years before final agreement could be reached to admit Belarus.
Among key questions the delegation is likely to face are the economic terms and conditions of a recent accord Lukashenko signed with Russian President Boris Yeltsin.

Russia itself has been negotiating entry for more than three years and Ukraine for a year. WTO officials say former communist states often fail to appreciate that admission is based on economic and not political criteria.

Applicants have to convince the 131 members of the WTO that their trade policies and practices as well as their markets are open to the outside world and that they are ready to bring their laws into line with WTO rules.

Of the 15 former republics of the old Soviet Union, 14 have applied to join the trade body -- in which members have to pledge non-discrimination in their trading relations with other members -- but none have yet been admitted.
The only ex-Soviet state not to apply so far is central Asian Turkmenistan.
